title: Reduced nodal subcurves and their reduced boundary intersection
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ be a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], pure of dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be a reduced closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], pure of dimension one. Suppose an open neighbourhood $N$ of $Y$ in $X$ is nodal: at every nonsmooth closed point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] its completed local ring is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $Z$ be the closure of $X\setminus Y$ with its reduced closed subscheme structure, and form the scheme-theoretic intersection $T=Y\cap Z$, defined locally by the sum of the two closed-subscheme ideals. Then $Y$ is nodal, in the same completed-local-ring sense. The scheme $T$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], possibly empty. Every point of $T$ is a node of $X$ and is a smooth point of each of $Y$ and $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), parts (1), (2)(a)--(c), applied to N; exchanging the two complementary subcurves gives smoothness also on Z. The proof is local near Y, so X need not be nodal away from Y.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes $N$ Noetherian and quasi-compact. It is reduced because its local rings are local rings of $X$. The finite-type condition is local on its source apart from quasi-compactness: restrict the finite-type charts of $X$ to principal affine opens inside $N$, and take a finite subcover. Thus $N$ is finite type over $k$. Since $Y\subseteq N$, it remains a reduced closed subscheme with exactly its original pure dimension one. If $N$ is empty, so are $Y$ and $T$, and every conclusion is vacuous; otherwise continue.

source.place: Tag 0E38 hypotheses; Tags 01T6 and 01OW/01OZ for Noetherian restriction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] with ambient scheme $X$, open $X$ and $n=1$. It says that every point of $N$ has local topological dimension $1$ in $X$. Apply [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components] to the locally Noetherian $X$ and its open $N$: every irreducible component of $N$ has dimension $1$. This supplies the ambient equidimensionality needed in both later applications; it is not inferred merely from openness in an arbitrary Noetherian curve.

Put $W=\overline{N\setminus Y}_{\mathrm{red}}$ inside $N$. Apply [lem-trf-complementary-pure-subcurve-components] to $(N,Y)$, using Steps 1 and 2. It gives that $W$ is reduced and pure of dimension one (possibly empty), and that the reduced complementary closure of $N\setminus W$ in $N$ is $Y$. Both opens $N\setminus Y$ and $N\setminus W$ are reduced: their local rings are those of the reduced $N$. Therefore [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] identifies their scheme-theoretic closures with $W$ and $Y$, respectively. This verifies the hypotheses and the actual complementary closed subscheme when the roles are exchanged.

The open immersion $j:X\setminus Y\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact: its inverse image in every affine open of $X$ is an open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme and is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. It is quasi-separated since it is an immersion with diagonal an isomorphism. Its source is reduced, so [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] identifies its scheme-theoretic image with the stated reduced closure $Z$. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] to $j$ and the open target $N$. Its restricted image is the scheme-theoretic closure of $N\setminus Y$, namely $W$ by Step 3. Thus $W=Z\cap N$ as closed subschemes of $N$. Because $Y\subseteq N$, summing the two restricted ideals identifies $Y\cap W$ with the entire scheme $T=Y\cap Z$, including its scheme structure.

Apply [lem-trf-stacks-nodal-closed-subcurve] to $N$ and $Y$. Steps 1 and 2 give reducedness, finite type and pure dimension one; the stated nodal hypothesis supplies its nonsmooth completed-local-ring condition. Here $k$ is algebraically closed, so closed-point residue fields are $k$ and the prescribed nodal completions have exactly the required coefficient field. The complementary scheme-theoretic closure is $W$ by Step 3, and $Y\cap W=T$ by Step 4. Conclusion (1) makes $Y$ nodal, (2)(a) gives a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$, (2)(b) makes every boundary point a node of $N$, and (2)(c) makes $Y$ smooth there. An open subscheme has the same local rings at its points, so those nodes are nodes of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (1), (2)(a)--(c); closed points over an algebraically closed field.

proof.text: A finite field extension of an algebraically closed field is the field itself: the minimal polynomial of any element is irreducible and splits into linear factors, hence has degree one. Consequently the spectra of the finite separable extensions obtained in Step 5 are copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. This also allows the empty disjoint union.

If $W$ is empty, then $T=Y\cap W$ is empty and the remaining smoothness assertion is vacuous. Otherwise apply [lem-trf-stacks-nodal-closed-subcurve] again with ambient $N$ and closed subcurve $W$. The ambient hypotheses were checked in Steps 1, 2 and 5; $W$ is reduced and pure one-dimensional by Step 3. Crucially, its complementary scheme-theoretic closure in $N$ is exactly $Y$, also by Step 3. Conclusion (2)(c) therefore says that $W$ is smooth at every point of $W\cap Y=T$. Finally $W=Z\cap N$ is an open subscheme of $Z$ by Step 4; their local rings and morphisms to $k$ agree in that neighbourhood, so this is smoothness of $Z$ at the boundary points.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (2)(c), applied to W after the complementary-closure identification.
